evidence.reason: `render_units` collects templates with `git ls-tree -r`, i.e. recursively, and filters only on `Path(source).name.startswith('crq-')`. Because the write loop keys the output path solely on `source.name`, two distinct sources with the same basename (e.g. `.../systemd/crq-repair.service` and `.../systemd/extra/crq-repair.service`) map to the same target: the later `atomic_bytes` silently overwrites the earlier rendered unit, `paths` returns duplicate entries, and downstream digest verification re-renders/compares only the surviving file content, so the collision is never surfaced and one template's rendered unit is dropped. That is an implementation error in existing fail-closed input handling (which already raises `ValueError` for unknown/absent runtime units), not a new requirement. The minimal fix is to reject duplicate basenames (raise `ValueError`) before `output.mkdir`/writing, leaving unique basenames rendering as today. Minor, routine repair; no owner decision needed since no deployed unit's content changes for the normal flat tree.
